raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With the unified cache external linker and MTP/EAGLE/DSpark draft KV (packed draft mapping from #37914), the first KV load that needs a cross-rank broadcast kills the whole TP group:

```
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not tuple
```

`_with_packed_draft_mapping()` in `linker_pool_assembler.py` maps one transfer layer to `(target_layer, draft_layer)` once draft layers are packed into the same transfer layer, so `pool.layer_mapping[layer_id]` can be a tuple. `LinkerMLADedupBroadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer()` still uses that value as an int index into the per-layer buffer list, so the very first broadcast raises and every rank in the group exits. The surrounding log hints point at CUDA graph capture or `--mem-fraction-static`, so it reads like an out-of-memory problem while memory is untouched.

Reproduced on a TP deployment running the external linker with MTP: KV restore aborts on the first cross-rank load, no request is ever served.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/linker_mla_dedup.py`: unwrap the mapping exactly the way `get_prepared_layer_range_meta()` in `linker_pool_assembler.py` already does (`[mapped] if isinstance(mapped, int) else list(mapped)`) and broadcast every packed physical layer, keeping the mapping order and using each physical layer's own row width.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_linker_mla_dedup_broadcast.py`: the test file is now a CPU-registered regression test (`register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`), formatted per the repo's ruff and isort rules. Coverage goes from 4 to 12 cases: int mapping, packed tuple mapping, sequence mapping, physical layer zero, sparse mapping, unmapped layer, pool missing from `prepared`, multiple buffer components, DSA dual-pool preparation and dispatch, packed and unpacked data round trips, and empty indices.
- The data round-trip cases build a real DSA pool group, broadcaster, index preparation and `_bcast_layer`, mocking only rank discovery and the communication primitive. Source and receiver use different physical slots, and the assertions check target KV, draft KV, indexer and non-selected rows across repeated reuse of the shared staging buffer.

Broadcasting the packed draft layer is not optional here: in dedup mode the non-source ranks never read the store themselves, so dropping the draft row raises nothing and leaves stale draft KV on those ranks, which decodes to silently wrong tokens.

## Accuracy Tests

The test file cannot be run through a normal `import sglang` in this environment (no GPU dependency stack installed), so the numbers below come from an isolated harness that compiles the real classes and functions from this worktree's AST and runs the real test file against them. `envs`, `PoolName` and the CI registration are loaded from the actual source files; tensors are real CPU PyTorch. This is not a full package-import run and not a distributed communication test.

Environment: Python 3.12.10, torch 2.15.0+cpu, pytest 9.2.0. Base: main at d82e124a9e plus this commit.

- This commit: `12 passed`, 3.20s.
- Same test file against the parent's broadcaster source (before the fix): `6 failed, 6 passed`. The failures include the reported `TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not tuple`, so the test reproduces the bug rather than only asserting the new loop shape.
- Negative check on the fix itself: shrinking the packed mapping to the target layer only (i.e. broadcasting everything except the draft layer) fails the packed DSA round trip with `Mismatched elements: 16 / 40`. The failure comes from comparing KV data, not from a call-count assertion.
- Both touched files: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean (ruff 0.15.1), `isort --check-only` clean (isort 7.0.0).
- `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` now passes on the test file — this hook was the failing required check (Lint) on the previous revision of this PR, because the file sat under `test/registered/` without a CI registry call.

Not rerun here, and not claimed: the `54 passed, 26 skipped` figure from the earlier revision of this PR, full `pre-commit`, the test under a normal `import sglang`, GPU/NCCL, and a real external-cache restore. CI needs a `run-ci` label from a maintainer to exercise the registered suite.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A, and no speed claim is made.

- No new GPU staging buffer: the existing `kv_staging` and its chunking primitives are reused, and per-layer sizes still come from each layer's own element width.
- Mapping normalization does allocate a small Python list per broadcast layer, so this is not a "zero allocation" change.
- For int mappings the sequence of `_bcast_layer` calls is unchanged; packed mappings now also broadcast the draft layer that was previously dropped. No performance measurement was taken on the restore path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `isort --check-only` clean on both files)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (12 CPU cases, registered for `base-a-test-cpu`)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing option or behavior documented elsewhere changes)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (see above; no throughput path touched, so no speed number is offered)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -0,0 +1,238 @@
+"""CPU regression tests for packed physical layers in linker MLA broadcasts."""
+
+import unittest
+from collections import deque
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import PoolName
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hybrid_cache.linker_pool_assembler import (
+    _build_dsa_device_pool_group,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.linker_mla_dedup import (
+    LinkerMLADedupBroadcaster,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _broadcaster(layer_mapping, *, components=1):
+    # Dispatch-only tests avoid constructing a real pool or process group.
+    broadcaster = LinkerMLADedupBroadcaster.__new__(LinkerMLADedupBroadcaster)
+    broadcaster.pools = {"kv": SimpleNamespace(layer_mapping=layer_mapping)}
+    broadcaster.buffers = {
+        "kv": [
+            [
+                torch.empty((4, 128), dtype=torch.uint8),
+                torch.empty((4, 256), dtype=torch.uint8),
+                torch.empty((4, 512), dtype=torch.uint8),
+            ]
+            for _ in range(components)
+        ]
+    }
+    broadcaster.kv_staging = torch.empty(4096, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    calls = []
+
+    def record(buffers, staging, indices, elem, layer_id):
+        calls.append((elem, layer_id))
+
+    broadcaster._bcast_layer = record
+    return broadcaster, calls
+
+
+def _dsa_pool_group(*, source):
+    def buffers(rows, width, layers, offset):
+        result = []
+        for layer in range(layers):
+            values = torch.arange(rows * width) + offset + layer * 31
+            result.append(
+                values.remainder(251).to(torch.uint8).reshape(rows, 1, width)
+                if source
+                else torch.full((rows, 1, width), 255, dtype=torch.uint8)
+            )
+        return result
+
+    target = SimpleNamespace(
+        page_size=2,
+        layer_num=2,
+        kv_buffer=buffers(10, 4, 2, 1),
+        index_k_with_scale_buffer=buffers(5, 6, 2, 71),
+    )
+    draft = SimpleNamespace(
+        page_size=2,
+        kv_buffer=buffers(10, 4, 1, 131),
+        index_k_with_scale_buffer=buffers(5, 6, 1, 191),
+    )
+    return _build_dsa_device_pool_group(target, 2, (draft,))
+
+
+def _data_broadcaster(pool_group, *, source):
+    # Use the real constructor, preparation and _bcast_layer. Only rank discovery
+    # and the communication primitive are mocked; no NCCL group is initialized.
+    with (
+        envs.SGLANG_MLA_DEDUP_CHUNK_TOKENS.override(1),
+        mock.patch(
+            "sglang.srt.mem_cache.mla_host_dedup.mla_dedup_rank_and_size",
+            return_value=(0, 2),
+        ),
+    ):
+        broadcaster = LinkerMLADedupBroadcaster(
+            pool_group, group=object(), src_global_rank=0
+        )
+    broadcaster.is_src = source
+    return broadcaster
+
+
+class TestLinkerMLADedupBroadcast(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_int_layer_mapping_broadcasts_one_physical_layer(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({0: 1})
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {"kv": (torch.tensor([1, 2]), None)})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [(256, 1)])
+
+    def test_packed_draft_tuple_broadcasts_every_physical_layer(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({0: (1, 2)})
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {"kv": (torch.tensor([1, 2]), None)})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [(256, 1), (512, 2)])
+
+    def test_unmapped_layer_broadcasts_nothing(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({1: 0})
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {"kv": (torch.tensor([1, 2]), None)})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_pool_missing_from_prepared_is_skipped(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({0: (0, 1)})
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_physical_layer_zero_is_not_skipped(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({0: 0})
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {"kv": (torch.tensor([1]), None)})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [(128, 0)])
+
+    def test_sequence_mapping_broadcasts_every_physical_layer(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({0: [0, 1, 2]})
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {"kv": (torch.tensor([1]), None)})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [(128, 0), (256, 1), (512, 2)])
+
+    def test_every_component_broadcasts_every_mapped_layer(self):
+        broadcaster, calls = _broadcaster({0: (1, 2)}, components=2)
+        broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, {"kv": (torch.tensor([1]), None)})
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [(256, 1), (512, 2)] * 2)
+
+    def test_dsa_prepare_preserves_rank_local_token_and_page_order(self):
+        broadcaster = _data_broadcaster(_dsa_pool_group(source=True), source=True)
+        slots = torch.tensor([6, 7, 0, 1])
+        prepared = broadcaster.prepare_broadcast(
+            {PoolName.KV: slots, PoolName.INDEXER: slots}, None
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(prepared[PoolName.KV][0], slots)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(prepared[PoolName.INDEXER][0], torch.tensor([3, 0]))
+
+    def test_dsa_broadcast_uses_each_pools_indices_and_row_width(self):
+        broadcaster = _data_broadcaster(_dsa_pool_group(source=True), source=True)
+        slots = torch.tensor([6, 7, 0, 1])
+        prepared = broadcaster.prepare_broadcast(
+            {PoolName.KV: slots, PoolName.INDEXER: slots}, None
+        )
+        with mock.patch.object(broadcaster, "_bcast_layer") as broadcast:
+            broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, prepared)
+
+        self.assertEqual(broadcast.call_count, 4)
+        for call, (name, width, layer) in zip(
+            broadcast.call_args_list,
+            [
+                (PoolName.KV, 4, 0),
+                (PoolName.KV, 4, 2),
+                (PoolName.INDEXER, 6, 0),
+                (PoolName.INDEXER, 6, 2),
+            ],
+        ):
+            self.assertIs(call.args[0], broadcaster.buffers[name][0])
+            self.assertIs(call.args[1], broadcaster.kv_staging)
+            self.assertIs(call.args[2], prepared[name][0])
+            self.assertEqual(call.args[3:], (width, layer))
+
+    def _assert_data_round_trip(self, layer_id):
+        source = _data_broadcaster(_dsa_pool_group(source=True), source=True)
+        receiver = _data_broadcaster(_dsa_pool_group(source=False), source=False)
+        source_slots = torch.tensor([6, 7, 0, 1])
+        receiver_slots = torch.tensor([2, 3, 8, 9])
+        source_prepared = source.prepare_broadcast(
+            {name: source_slots for name in source.pools}, None
+        )
+        receiver_prepared = receiver.prepare_broadcast(
+            {name: receiver_slots for name in receiver.pools}, None
+        )
+        snapshots = {
+            name: [buf.clone() for buf in components[0]]
+            for name, components in receiver.buffers.items()
+        }
+        payloads = deque()
+
+        def send(tensor, *, src, group):
+            self.assertEqual(src, source.src_global_rank)
+            self.assertIs(group, source.group)
+            payloads.append(tensor.clone())
+
+        def receive(tensor, *, src, group):
+            self.assertEqual(src, receiver.src_global_rank)
+            self.assertIs(group, receiver.group)
+            payload = payloads.popleft()
+            self.assertEqual(tensor.shape, payload.shape)
+            tensor.copy_(payload)
+
+        # Eight staging bytes hold two KV rows but only one indexer row. Both
+        # pools need two chunks per physical layer, reusing the same staging.
+        self.assertEqual(source.kv_staging.numel(), 8)
+        with mock.patch.object(torch.distributed, "broadcast", side_effect=send):
+            source.broadcast_loaded_layer(layer_id, source_prepared)
+        chunk_count = len(payloads)
+        with mock.patch.object(torch.distributed, "broadcast", side_effect=receive):
+            receiver.broadcast_loaded_layer(layer_id, receiver_prepared)
+        self.assertEqual(len(payloads), 0)
+
+        for name, pool in source.pools.items():
+            mapped = pool.layer_mapping[layer_id]
+            layers = [mapped] if isinstance(mapped, int) else list(mapped)
+            for layer, received in enumerate(receiver.buffers[name][0]):
+                expected = snapshots[name][layer]
+                if layer in layers:
+                    expected.index_copy_(
+                        0,
+                        receiver_prepared[name][0],
+                        source.buffers[name][0][layer].index_select(
+                            0, source_prepared[name][0]
+                        ),
+                    )
+                # Compare the entire buffer: non-selected rows and unmapped
+                # layers must retain their sentinel values.
+                torch.testing.assert_close(received, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        self.assertEqual(chunk_count, 8 if layer_id == 0 else 4)
+
+    def test_packed_dsa_data_round_trip_with_rank_local_slots_and_chunking(self):
+        self._assert_data_round_trip(0)
+
+    def test_int_dsa_data_round_trip_with_rank_local_slots_and_chunking(self):
+        self._assert_data_round_trip(1)
+
+    def test_empty_indices_issue_no_collectives_and_leave_buffers_untouched(self):
+        broadcaster = _data_broadcaster(_dsa_pool_group(source=False), source=False)
+        empty = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64)
+        prepared = broadcaster.prepare_broadcast(
+            {name: empty for name in broadcaster.pools}, None
+        )
+        with mock.patch.object(torch.distributed, "broadcast") as broadcast:
+            broadcaster.broadcast_loaded_layer(0, prepared)
+        broadcast.assert_not_called()
+        for components in broadcaster.buffers.values():
+            for buffer in components[0]:
